name: GMVN Tourist Rest House Devprayag
why_it_matters: The state-run Garhwal Mandal rest house is the most reliable hot meal in town — 14 rooms and a small canteen kitchen serving home-style thalis to pilgrims and Char Dham travellers since the colonial-era guesthouse was first built. The simplest test of Devprayag's pure-veg pilgrim-town norm: no menu theatre, just dal-chawal-sabzi.
insider_tip: Lunch and dinner are fixed-time (roughly 1pm and 8pm); arrive within the window or you'll get cold leftovers. Non-residents are usually served if there's capacity — ask at reception, not the kitchen.
signature_address: GMVN Tourist Rest House, Devprayag, Pauri Garhwal, Uttarakhand 246186

name: Alpenrose Restaurant (The Tattva)
why_it_matters: The only fine-dining room in or around Devprayag — 60 seats inside The Tattva resort overlooking the Bhagirathi-Alaknanda confluence. Pure-vegetarian by design (matching the sangam's religious code), with a buffet that puts Garhwali staples like chainsu and kafuli alongside continental fare. As close to a Char Dham luxury halt as the area offers.
insider_tip: Non-resident diners are welcome but should call ahead — the buffet is sized for in-house guests and walk-ins get à la carte only. Breakfast (7-10am) is the best-value sitting if you want the river view without committing to a stay.
signature_address: The Tattva, Village Dansara, Pant Gaon, Devprayag, Uttarakhand 249301

name: Hotel Ganga Vista Restaurant
why_it_matters: Roadside hotel-restaurant on the Rishikesh-Badrinath highway approach to Devprayag, opposite the Indian Oil petrol pump. Pure-veg multi-cuisine kitchen running North Indian, South Indian and Garhwali sections in parallel — geared to Char Dham buses and Jain pilgrims who need onion-garlic-free options on the route.
insider_tip: The South Indian counter is the unexpected pick — they keep the dosa batter ready through the day for tour-bus halts, so a 3pm masala dosa lands in five minutes when most kitchens are between meal services.
signature_address: Opposite Indian Oil Petrol Pump, Badrinath Highway, Pant Gaon, Devprayag, Uttarakhand 249301

name: Hotel Pious Ganga Restaurant
why_it_matters: Highway-side budget hotel with an in-house kitchen 650m from the Devprayag View Point — one of the few sit-down dining rooms inside the town strip itself, as opposed to the Pant Gaon approach. Pure-veg, walk-in, sized for Char Dham travellers stopping for a thali before pushing to Srinagar or Rudraprayag.
insider_tip: Pricing is on-request and varies with the yatra season — confirm thali rate before ordering, as April-October sees Char Dham mark-ups. Stick to dal-roti-sabzi; the kitchen is small and dishes outside that core take 30+ minutes.
signature_address: Hotel Pious Ganga, NH-58, Haridwar Rishikesh Badrinath Road, Devprayag, Uttarakhand 249201
